rationale: Follow-up discriminator for the same investigation: installSnapshot already calls removeOldLogs for a MonotonicLogStore, which deletes the above-snapshot log bytes, whereas for a non-monotonic store it only compacts at or below the snapshot index. Running both store types with the same stale suffix separates 'retained log bytes' from 'the cached last-log index/term' as the cause of the catch-up stall. This is a changed harness (new scenario and field) so it takes a successor with a fresh execution.

scope.description: One process, three real Raft instances over InmemTransport with FileSnapshotStore; each scenario selects InmemStore either directly (non-monotonic) or wrapped in MockMonotonicLogStore (monotonic) via MakeClusterCustom. The replacement leader compacts at or below its snapshot index (TrailingLogs=0).
assumptions: Config: ProtocolVersion=3, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=300ms, CommitTimeout=10ms, TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold disabled, SnapshotInterval=1h.
The isolated node's above-snapshot suffix is produced by real uncommitted Apply calls on the old leader before it steps down; no state is injected.
MockMonotonicLogStore returns IsMonotonic()==true, so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch.
excluded: Network and TCP transports; mixed-version rolling upgrades.
Restart or recovery of the isolated node; only live catch-up is measured.
Disk-backed stores (the in-memory stores share the same LogStore contract).

experiment.prefix: For each of three scenarios: bootstrap a 3-node cluster, commit a 20-command prefix, isolate the current leader, append 2 (control) or 200 (both stall cases) uncommitted tail commands on the isolated node, let the remaining two nodes elect a replacement leader, commit 20 more commands and take a snapshot at index S, commit 10 post entries above S, reconnect, and observe for about 4.5s. The two stall scenarios differ only in the isolated node's log store (non-monotonic vs MockMonotonicLogStore).
experiment.requirement: After a follower installs a snapshot at index S, catch-up must not depend on whether the above-S bytes survive: regardless of the LogStore's monotonicity, a follower whose persisted log ended above S must stop reporting a last log entry above S and accept the leader's AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=S so it converges to the leader's log. Anchored in state.go:167-174 (getLastEntry) and raft.go:1475-1502 (appendEntries PrevLogEntry check); installSnapshot at raft.go:1814-1953 chooses removeOldLogs for a MonotonicLogStore and compactLogs otherwise, and is the producer responsible for the post-install last-log state.
experiment.responsibility: Follower snapshot installation establishing a post-install last-log state compatible with the leader's AppendEntries and nextIndex catch-up loop, for both monoticity branches of the LogStore.

comparisons.description: Control: isolated log at or below the snapshot index reaches the leader commit index.
Non-monotonic store with a stale above-snapshot suffix must still catch up; the retained run shows it stalls.
Monotonic store with a stale above-snapshot suffix: removeOldLogs deletes the bytes, yet the cached last-log state must not block catch-up; the retained run shows it still stalls.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a third scenario using MakeClusterCustom with MonotonicLogs=true so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch, plus a store_monotonic field and a corresponding comparison. The control and the non-monotonic stall scenario are unchanged. This isolates whether the stall is caused by retained above-snapshot log bytes or by the cached last-log index/term.
